claims.text: The Qarakhanid account identifies the western khagan’s seat at Samarkand, ruling-clan appanages and subsequent western-khanate subordination to the Seljuqs after Malik Shah’s 1089 intervention.

Earlier khagan/appanage and Borhan sadr/governor/tribute relations remain distinct. Selected 1000–1213 includes separately attributed 1207 and 1209–10/1212–13 acts, not common 1200 government. Disputed 1198 and division circa 1040/1046 are unresolved;1217–18 deposition excluded. Iranica scholarship/working English; cited originals uncollated.

claims.text: Iranica distinguishes Samarkand’s western khagan and clan appanages from Bukhara’s Borhan governors and tribute collectors. Its later accounts separately describe Bukhara’s negotiated entry and citadel work in 1207, the western ruler’s surrender in 1209–10 and the khanate’s end in 1212–13. The explicitly extended selection preserves those distinct acts; neither one dynasty label nor these dates establishes identical offices, common government in 1200 or popular assent. Originals remain uncollated.
